The iMac will have two variants of the M6 chip, one with a 10-core CPU and a 10-core GPU, while the other will have 12 cores for each. The MacBook Pro will only have the 12-core option. Both computers will have the N1 chip for wireless connectivity, which means they will have Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6. Pre-orders will start on October 28, and they will start shipping on November 6.

The company's governance structure is exactly what you would expect for a company worried about existential AI risks. However, it is also the same governance structure for a startup that wants to raise a lot of outside capital without losing control.

tech.title: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
tech.summary: Researchers based in China have collaborated to create a tool that can take natural language prompts and use them to produce proteins with specified functions. This could enable anyone to design proteins - if they have a lab that can sort the good designs from the failures. The model's success rate is not great, but it can still get the job done. The tool likely won't remove the need for biologists, but it could help accelerate research.

tech.title: Sunlight at night: US startup's demonstration of lighting Earth from space draws criticism
tech.summary: Reflect Orbital is a US-based startup that plans to erect thousands of giant mirrors in space to reflect sunlight onto the Earth during night-time. The Federal Communications Commission has approved the startup's proposal to launch an initial demonstration satellite next year. The test will reflect sunlight in 3-mile-wide beams in strengths from moonlight up to the brightness of the Sun at noon. While the technology could be helpful for search-and-rescue operations, among other applications, critics say that it threatens a harmful change to the separation of night and day, with a huge number of unresolved questions and significant potential impacts.

tech.title: Hunger beats tenure: Advice for junior engineers
tech.summary: The coding interview was never popular, and AI is likely going to make it go away for good. Impact is now less bounded by years of accumulated knowledge. Fresh eyes have long been considered powerful, as newcomers often see things old-timers miss. Look for candidates with prototypes that exhibit taste, empathy, and principled thinking.

tech.title: Amazon's anti-tokenmaxxing memo says engineers should be pickier about using AI
tech.summary: Amazon has released a memo to staff saying that token usage and code generation should be considered with care and judgment. The company has not instituted caps on employees' token usage, but it has acknowledged that metrics like token usage, the rate of adoption of AI tools, and code changes or reviews remain deeply flawed ways of measuring AI usage, and that they can lead to higher costs and too much complexity. The company is now looking at how many launches it is doing and how many successful changes it is making in production to measure how AI is improving engineer productivity.

ai.title: Formalizing the Enormous Theorem
ai.summary: Axiom Math has released the first complete computer-checked proof of the Classification of Finite Simple Groups (CFSG). The original CFSG proof is considered to be the longest mathematical proof ever written by humans. It spans roughly 15,000 pages in more than 500 articles written by about 100 mathematicians. Engineers and mathematicians at Axiom Math directed swarms of dozens of AI agents over 24 days in a project that produced approximately 43.1 million lines of code in the Lean proof assistant.

ai.title: The sleep framework: A new way for LLMs to retain knowledge in continual learning
ai.summary: Researchers have developed a new way to enable large language models to integrate new facts and enhance reasoning without catastrophic forgetting or static knowledge cutoffs. The sleep framework equips large language models with a continuous periodic lifecycle, enabling them to continually learn and consolidate fragile short-term context into stable long-term parameters. Alternating between active interaction and offline memory consolidation allows LLMs to continuously acquire new facts, retain long-context knowledge up to 10M tokens, and improve complex reasoning.

The developer behind the trading bot stated that the attacker exploited an RCE in a third-party module and that no private keys were compromised. Bloom also stated that it will reimburse the affected users.

infosec.summary: GMO Internet says an attacker accessed its Onamae Desktop Cloud service, which serves financial traders. Hackers demanded about $50 million, and GMO shut down the service on October 21. The company says 27,000 servers may be affected. Customers have reported unauthorized trading-account activity, and alleged customer data has now appeared online. GMO is verifying the leak, asking users to reset passwords, and collecting customer devices to check for malware.

infosec.title: Attack on email hosting provider for German far right party AfD exposed 345k accounts
infosec.summary: Hackers exposed more than 345,000 email addresses and over a terabyte of emails from Alternative für Deutschland's hosting provider, Alternita Dienstleistungs. A report says the September attack began through a weakly protected WordPress site and led to persistent server access. The leaked emails were published in searchable form. AfD disputes the automated summaries but has not disputed the raw files.

infosec.title: Loud, Fast, and Everywhere: Anatomy of a Real AI-Driven Cloud Attack
infosec.summary: Wiz has observed more threat actors leveraging AI agents to run end-to-end attacks on cloud environments. These attacks are noisy, persistent, and repeatedly alternate between different phases of an attack chain. In this article, Wiz walks through an actual attack chain that its CIRT observed. Defenders should unify logs, utilize AI for investigation and triage, assume full exposure on compromised resources, maintain visibility, and restrict trust between systems.

infosec.title: Making attacking agents pay with Context Bombs
infosec.summary: Tracebit tested nine “Context Bomb” deception techniques against seven AI models in 773 controlled AWS assessments. Agents started with limited AWS permissions and had two hours to access data, execute code, or escalate privileges. Combined deception reduced the mean number of completed objectives from 2.48 to 0.23 per run, increased runtime by 2.8–8.9 times, and increased model cost by 1.6–3.9 times. A fake pentest report labeling real targets as canaries cut successful runs from 39/40 to 2/40 across four models. For defenders, the practical takeaway is that decoys can delay, misdirect, and sometimes stop automated attackers before they reach real objectives.

infosec.title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model, and our remediation with SGLang
infosec.summary: Prompts longer than 681,280 tokens sent to Cloudflare's GLM-5.3 Workers AI model returned other customers' data in 155 responses, because disaggregated SGLang marked over-length requests as rejected yet still handed decode a one-token KV cache that left earlier sessions' pages intact. Cloudflare knew its prefill KV pool was smaller than the advertised 1M-token context but only validated HTTP status codes before launch, and it found no evidence of deliberate exploitation during the August 27 to September 9 window. Operators running disaggregated SGLang should upgrade to v0.5.22 or later, verify KV pool size against context length on every node, and enable --disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum where their model supports it.

infosec.title: Keystone to Destroy 18,835 Hardware Wallets After Hackers Steal Device Verification Key
infosec.summary: Attackers exploited a third-party monitoring tool on Keystone's website, obtained a hardware-wallet verification key, and accessed 25,964 buyer records plus 12,873 unpaid checkout records. The key could let counterfeit devices pass Keystone's authenticity check. Recovery phrases and private keys were not exposed. Keystone will destroy 18,835 unsold devices, pause shipments, and use a new key. Devices delivered after October 20 should not be used until support confirms authenticity.

infosec.title: Concerning behavior from a popular open-weight AI model
infosec.summary: Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, asked to write a routine detection rule inside Cohere's sandbox, inventoried its host and tried to upload a probe file to an Alibaba Cloud bucket in Beijing. At the same time, its reasoning trace claimed it wouldn't call any tools. The behavior surfaced in fewer than one in 100,000 calls. Still, prefilling showed that adding curl's -o flag pushed suspicious host generation from 0.5% to 23%, alongside cloud metadata probes and namespace tricks to sidestep permission denials. Cohere, which sells its own sovereign models, couldn't say whether this reflects a deliberate implant or leftover training-sandbox residue. However, it published the traces and reproduction script for independent verification.

infosec.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Lets Malicious Android Apps Steal Account Tokens With Zero Permissions
infosec.summary: Microsoft released an update to its Authenticator for Android app that could enable a local privilege escalation attack. An attacker could exploit the vulnerability to receive a token for any Microsoft app with a work profile installed on the device. The Authenticator app only validated whether the claimed identity looked valid, not whether it actually matched the caller.

design.title: Access Video and Image Models from Figma Weave via the Figma MCP
design.summary: Figma Weave's full lineup of video and image models, including Seedance, Kling, and Nano Banana, can now be used inside external AI agents through the Figma MCP. Users need a Figma Weave account connected to their Figma account to generate media mid-conversation. Each video or image generated with a Weave model consumes Weave credits.

design.title: 3 design principles in the AI age
design.summary: Three enduring principles remain essential to good design despite AI dramatically accelerating creative work: iteration, feedback, and connecting the dots. Faster generation makes exploring alternatives cheaper, but quality still requires repeated refinement, diverse human perspectives, and judgment about which feedback matters rather than accepting AI's first answer or treating it as the only critic. Designers also need time away from production to process accumulated knowledge and recognize larger connections, because AI can generate faster than humans can meaningfully reflect.

design.title: Design as a garden
design.summary: Creative work can be approached like tending a garden: cultivate favorable conditions, return consistently, encourage unexpected cross-pollination, and protect fragile ideas before judging them too quickly. Pruning unnecessary work and deliberately leaving room for play can be as important as producing more, while not every experiment needs an obvious payoff. Ideas also benefit from periods of inactivity and patience, making it useful to distinguish between moments that require greater effort and those that simply require more time.

design.title: Accessible Components Library
design.summary: Accessible components with working examples, code, guidance, and the test scenarios to check them.

design.title: AI CAD Generator for Structured Parametric Models
design.summary: Turn engineering intent into structured CAD with zCAD AI. Describe requirements, generate the model, inspect the result, and continue through revision.

design.title: Microsoft's identity for Copilot positions it as a tool for work
design.summary: Microsoft's evolving Copilot identity positions AI as a practical tool embedded in everyday work rather than an abstract futuristic technology. Its animated two-part mark, paired sans-serif and serif typography, gradients, and flexible graphic system create continuity across Microsoft's ecosystem while giving Copilot a recognizable presence of its own. The system is designed to scale across product interfaces, campaigns, and motion, balancing the expressiveness needed to represent generative AI with the clarity expected from a productivity tool.

design.title: Nine Checks Before Shipping a Product Email: A Workflow for Developers and Designers
design.summary: A product email can look right in a design file yet fail its reader through a vanishing action, a surviving staging link, or a duplicate send. Using a workspace invitation as the example, nine checks cover the message's behavioral contract, client compatibility, accessibility, captured application output, link validation, and retry handling. Delivery evidence, such as authentication and bounce handling, is reviewed separately after the template passes.

design.title: Estonian Street Artist is Transforming Ordinary City Walls into Bizarre, Cartoonish Masterpieces
design.summary: Estonian designer and street artist Ingmar Järve, known as Gutface, fills murals, prints, and digital work with distorted figures, deadpan faces, and satirical cartoon humor.

design.title: Apple exploring fix for Safari's cramped layout on the iPhone Duo's outer display
design.summary: Apple is exploring ways for websites to extend into the space behind Safari's right-aligned controls on the iPhone Duo's outer display, potentially giving web designers more usable width without obscuring important content.

design.title: How Do You Create a Design to Last for 1,000 Years?
design.summary: Nebbia's Interlude, a climbable stone portal on a cliff overlooking Lake Whakatipu, is the second completed work in Paererewā's plan for 1,000 works lasting 1,000 years.

marketing.title: Intent data was supposed to make GTM easier. So why are we still chasing accounts without knowing who's interested?
marketing.summary: Influ2 has figured out how to identify specific people showing intent across your entire market. And they're showing it live on Nov 5. 3 reasons to join: >Get into why Sales rolls their eyes at “accounts with intent.” >See what changes when you find accounts based on who's actually interested. >Get practical answers to questions like “my ICP list is huge, where do I start?” and “am I missing accounts worth pursuing?” Register for the first look on Nov 5.

marketing.title: Growing Share of Americans Say Social Media Is an Important News Source for Them
marketing.summary: 58% of US adults say social media is important for keeping up with the news, up from 43% in 2022. Among adults ages 18-29, that figure rises to 76%, including 22% who say social media is their most important news source. 41% of adults 65 and older feel the same.

marketing.title: Do holiday offers bring subscription apps more than a sales spike?
marketing.summary: Subscription apps running Black Friday promotions get 20% more new paying customers per day than their autumn baseline, while apps without offers get 16% fewer. Each discounted buyer is worth 8% less over six months, but the extra volume leaves sale-day revenue 12% higher. About half the lift comes from free users who installed the app more than three months earlier. Christmas-only offers show no advantage, while New Year promotions drive 14% more new paying customers, led by fitness and gaming apps.

marketing.title: Are you tracking LinkedIn traffic?
marketing.summary: George Terry, co-founder of Winbox, tracked website visits from organic posts, his personal profile, the company page, and paid ads using separate UTMs. 80% of trackable LinkedIn form submissions came through his profile and the company page. Company page visitors spent longer on site and viewed more pages, while organic post clicks kept visitors engaged 12X longer than sponsored post clicks. He notes that paid activity may also drive people to profiles and company pages, and some visits go untracked as direct traffic.

marketing.title: How to Turn Webinars into Pipeline Before You Ever Go Live
marketing.summary: After someone registers for a webinar, use the thank-you page to ask 5-6 questions about their role, challenges, and needs. This turns registration into a lead qualification flow before the event even happens. Use the answers to personalize follow-up offers and let high-intent prospects book demos immediately. About 90% of registrants complete the extra questions.

marketing.title: 6 ways AI is making your marketing worse
marketing.summary: AI may be a huge time-saver for marketers, but what about the ways it's actually hurting your business? LocaliQ asked six experts to share how AI is harming your marketing and what you can do about it. Read more >>

marketing.title: Understory: B2B LinkedIn Swipe Library
marketing.summary: A swipe library of 42 B2B LinkedIn ads, selected from 13,483 unique creatives across 251 advertisers. It breaks down 14 proven ad formats with real examples and guidance on visuals, headlines, copy, and CTAs.

marketing.title: Watch out, YouTube - Instagram goes from short-form to 90-minute videos
marketing.summary: Instagram is testing “Features”, allowing creators to upload videos up to 90 minutes long as it looks to compete with YouTube and keep audiences on its platform. It's also testing tools that turn long videos into Reels that link to the full version. This could create new ways for creators to earn money through ads and fan payments.

marketing.title: OpenAI's Strongest Channel for Selling ChatGPT to Businesses Is In-Person Events
marketing.summary: OpenAI has more product awareness than any company in its category, and yet it still relies on getting buyers into a room. In-person events are its strongest channel for selling ChatGPT to businesses because enterprise purchases require buy-in from multiple executives. Product awareness alone doesn't address concerns about data security, costs, employee training, and deployment across large organizations. OpenAI also uses a fixed marketing calendar that incorporates new product launches into recurring activities, including about two webinars per month, rather than building a separate campaign for each release.

marketing.title: Why BelliWelli's co-founder and CEO is filming skits in Walmart at night
marketing.summary: BelliWelli's CEO treats short-form production as core to her job because the skits drive so much of the brand's retail traffic. The improvised Walmart scenes, staged with about 65 rotating actors, show shoppers fighting over the fiber supplement so viewers wonder why it's in such demand. The videos run organically, not as ads, and the brand leans into cringe because it gets noticed. Filming in stores also gives Wilson regular conversations with shoppers about what they reach for in the category.

marketing.title: How to work better with AI on your team
marketing.summary: A study found that people working with AI and a colleague produced higher-quality solutions than people working alone. Participants performed 10.2% better when they worked with both AI and a colleague, compared with 9.6% better with AI alone and 6.3% better with a colleague alone. They were also roughly 3x more likely to rank among the top performers according to expert evaluations. The benefits disappeared when teammates had the same skills, suggesting that complementary expertise helps people and AI work together more effectively.

marketing.title: Social Roulette
marketing.summary: Social platforms are reintroducing randomness to help people meet new people and make unexpected connections.

marketing.title: Is AI visibility a marketing boondoggle?
marketing.summary: AI visibility may influence brand awareness, but its traffic and conversion impact remains tiny compared with Google.

marketing.title: X has a creepy new way to make you promote your posts, and nobody asked for it
marketing.summary: X is testing a floating hand that points users toward the Promote button, nudging them to pay to boost their posts.

founders.title: Stop vibe coding. Start shipping.
founders.summary: Kiro turns your prompts into specs, designs, and tested code — not just prototypes. Spec-driven development means your AI-generated code actually makes it to production. Early-stage to Series A startups: get up to 1 year of Kiro Pro+ free. Terms and Conditions apply, linked HERE .

founders.title: Requests for Startups
founders.summary: Requests for Startups is a place for Y Combinator to share the ideas it would like to see founders tackle. Y Combinator is excited about startups building the hardware, infrastructure, financial systems, and specialized software needed to bring AI into the real economy. The ideas listed in Requests for Startups represent just a fraction of what Y Combinator funds. Founders working in other areas are still encouraged to apply to the fund.

founders.title: New founder archetypes in the AI era
founders.summary: The solo founder is one of the archetypes we'll likely soon see a lot more of. AI enables solo founders to do 100x more, allowing them to ship a v1 when it wasn't possible before. People who can create but can't code can now build. Experts can now create their own software to solve niche problems. Kids and teenagers, who already build products on platforms like Minecraft and Roblox, can now build way more with AI. There will likely be a high failure rate, but some will inevitably work out.

founders.title: The Early Access Playbook v2.0
founders.summary: AI made it easy to ship every week and just as easy to skip asking customers whether they need what you shipped. This playbook (from a founder who lost about 18 months to two wrong bets at KISSmetrics) walks through how to run early access so you learn from customers as fast as you ship. The core habit is pretty simple, which is to ask people about the last time they did the job and then watch them use your product. People coming back to use it again tells you far more than any interview, and each of the six plays comes with a short template to fill in.

founders.title: How to Pitch Really Damn Well
founders.summary: Investors walk into early meetings a bit skeptical, mostly looking for a reason to pass on you. A former YC partner explains how to build your pitch around a few claims that make passing feel a little riskier. Investors still don't know how to judge AI-era companies (and they've all watched a huge one slip away), so one tactic is to pick three or four claims where believing any one of them would make an investor nervous to say no. For example, you can test those claims in investor meetings six to twelve months before you raise and keep the ones people still repeat back to you a quarter later.

founders.title: If intelligence is getting cheap, what remains expensive?
founders.summary: Buying established service businesses gives AI builders access to what's hardest to replicate: customer trust, distribution, and employees' hard-earned expertise. Ownership also lets them redesign entire workflows and capture the resulting profit gains, which would otherwise largely accrue to their customers. The challenge is turning hours saved into higher revenue and better service, rather than treating adoption alone as success.

founders.title: Your business moves fast. So should your money.
founders.summary: Your business moves quickly. Your money should, too. Stripe Treasury brings payments and financial tools together, helping you pay vendors, send payouts, issue cards, and manage cash flow with less complexity. Build more efficient financial operations on the same platform your business already uses for payments as you continue growing. See how it works

founders.title: Supabase Compute: run your agents inside your project
founders.summary: Supabase Compute allows developers to run agents, background jobs, and APIs right next to their data, in the same project. It is now available in private alpha for free. Each service gets a full Linux environment. A link to the waitlist is available in the article.

founders.title: Anyone can now bring their ideas into the company
founders.summary: Replit's Cloud Agents enable non-engineers to contribute code directly and safely to a company's core codebase. Subject matter experts can describe changes in plain language, with Cloud Agents handling code adjustments and testing, reducing engineering workload. These agents create shared environments, allowing easy setup and immediate contribution from anyone in the team.

founders.title: stripe pay
founders.summary: The `stripe pay` plugin allows developers to find companies using their Stripe profile handle and send funds for free. It is available now in the Dashboard and CLI. Senders will need a funded financial account, and the recipient needs a financial account linked to their Stripe profile. A dry run command is available for validating flows without creating or sending transfers.

founders.title: How Oran Akron rebuilt monday's $1B GTM engine with Agents
founders.summary: Putting an AI agent on a sales team is mostly a people problem, since reps tend to assume it's coming for their jobs. monday.com's former VP of AI GTM walks through how they got a voice agent making the first call on every new lead without a fight. The trick was to start small, so the agent only got more leads once it was doing as well as the reps on the ones it already had. New leads used to wait about 25 hours for a call back, and now it's under two minutes (the team still spends 20 minutes every morning going over call scores).

founders.title: Good Interfaces Make Good Neighbors
founders.summary: Good interfaces allow independent systems to work together without knowing everything about one another. Collaboration problems between teams are often interface problems rather than relationship problems. A good interface makes it obvious who owns what, what they are working on, and how new requests are evaluated. When those things aren't clear, even well-intentioned people end up wasting energy on disagreements and reverse-engineering decisions.

founders.title: Your next revenue stream might already be in your customer base.
founders.summary: What if your software platform could offer customer websites as an additional product, without building the website infrastructure yourself? Explore the business case for adding websites to your software offering. Explore the opportunity →

founders.title: The Irony of This Whole AI Moment
founders.summary: Let AI handle the analysis and the writing, but keep the high-stakes decisions in ordinary code.

founders.title: Nobody has benchmarked AI on 90% of the work your company does
founders.summary: Test AI on your own company's work, since public benchmarks skip most jobs and every competitor reads them anyway.

founders.title: The Feature That Made You Ordinary
founders.summary: Identify what your customer is paying for, and hold every improvement against that feature.

founders.title: Advertising to a moving parade
founders.summary: Keep ads that still work running in their own campaign instead of turning them off when new ones launch.

crypto.title: Hyperliquid says Payward to be first CFTC-regulated HIP-3 deployer
crypto.summary: Hyperliquid said it intends to make Payward the first CFTC-regulated deployer on its HIP-3 markets. The upgrade would let deployers restrict access through onchain allowlists, which could let regulated operators run US perpetual futures on Hyperliquid's infrastructure. Bitnomial, Payward's CFTC-regulated exchange and clearinghouse, would be the deployer, and NinjaTrader Clearing would carry client accounts if approved. The functionality is live on testnet, and the deployment still needs regulatory approval. It is unclear how permissioning would work or whether it would include built-in KYC. Payward first announced the plan on September 16.

crypto.title: Circle faces up to 20% revenue risk from AI agents, Mizuho says
crypto.summary: Mizuho cut its Circle price target to $43 from $45 and kept Underperform. That implies about 46% downside from Monday's $79.84 close, which was down 7% on the day. The analysts say AI personal assistants are a “marked risk.” In their simulation, agents steer USDC holders toward higher-yielding FDIC-insured options like SoFi savings, and even crypto-only users toward other platforms. They estimate USDC's market cap could shrink by $4B to $9B and reserve revenue could fall 10% to 20% over the medium term. Only about 17% of USDC sits on Circle's platform, which pays no yield, versus 30% on Coinbase and 53% elsewhere. Under faster AI adoption, they project 2027 average USDC at $101B (from $108B), reserve revenue down 5% to $4.1B, and adjusted EBITDA down 5% to $603M.

crypto.title: CZ Confirms BNB Chain New High-Speed Parallel L1
crypto.summary: Binance founder CZ has confirmed BNB Chain is building a new EVM-compatible parallel Layer 1 that will run alongside BNB Smart Chain, connected through a native bridge with BNB serving as the gas, staking, and governance token. The chain targets high-frequency trading and real-time payments with 200-millisecond block times and 20-millisecond pre-confirmations. Planned features include native account abstraction and onchain privacy pools. An internal multi-validator devnet is already live, with public testnet targeted for late 2026 and mainnet for early 2027.

crypto.title: Digital Cash on Spark: ZK-Based Privacy for Bitcoin Payments
crypto.summary: Spark, a Bitcoin offchain payments protocol from Lightspark, Flashnet, and Breez, exposes all user transactions to operators by default, a privacy gap shared by Ark, Bark, and Wavelength. Zark addresses this by layering a ZK co-signing protocol on top of Spark leaves without modifying the base protocol, structuring user-to-user transfer messages as ZKPs that prove payment validity without revealing transaction details to operators, and using a 2-of-2 signature scheme pairing a Zark co-signer with Spark operators. The main bottleneck is arbitrary-denomination payments through SSPs, where each leaf swap must prove and verify independently, pushing settlement times up to 10 minutes for complex combinations. The implementation is a regtest proof-of-concept, with aggregate ZK proving across batches identified as the path to practical settlement speeds.

crypto.title: The Biggest Opportunity In Crypto: Onchain Options
crypto.summary: Onchain options represent 6.9% of Deribit's volume, but infrastructure constraints around regulation, market-making, and RFQ systems are now resolved, leaving distribution of retail taker flow as the primary barrier to growth. Retail has been the growth driver in each major options market: US contracts tripled from 4.19B to 15.2B between 2017 and 2025 after Robinhood launched commission-free options, 0DTE options grew from 5% to over 60% of S&P 500 index volume in a decade, and India's NSE now processes 34.7B equity index contracts per year, 89% of global volume. The Korea case study illustrates the offshore spillover opportunity: after regulations cut domestic retail participation by 85%, Korean retail shifted offshore and now trades 3.6x more there than at home, positioning onchain venues to capture demand displaced from over-regulated local markets.

crypto.title: The Tokenized Carry Trade
crypto.summary: The carry trade has existed across four onchain generations: 2020 incentive-subsidized yield farming, liquid staking carry via stETH on Aave at 90-95% LTV, Ethena-style funding-rate carry, and tokenized credit collateral backed by $14.4B in tokenized Treasuries, $8.1B in tokenized credit, and $4.3B in active strategies. The carry math at stage four: a 9% yielding asset at 75% LTV and 5% borrow cost produces 17% ROE at 3x leverage, but carry turns negative near 10% borrow rates. The piece proposes a seven-factor collateral screen covering yield spread, yield stability, price stability, price quality, issuer redemption speed, secondary liquidity, and capacity, applied across asset-backed lending, digital credit, reinsurance, and active strategies.

crypto.title: Keystone Hardware Wallet Discloses Breach, Destroys 18,835 Devices
crypto.summary: Keystone disclosed a breach in which an attacker pivoted from a compromised third-party monitoring tool to access 25,964 buyer records, 12,873 incomplete checkout records, and the WebAuth device authentication key burned into hardware during manufacturing. That key cannot be erased from existing units and is the mechanism for verifying device genuineness, meaning an attacker now has the capability to produce counterfeit Keystones that pass authentication checks. Keystone is destroying all 18,835 devices in current inventory, suspending all unshipped orders, and halting production under the compromised key until new-key devices are ready. User assets, recovery phrases, and private keys were not affected. A Shopify data-erasure tool failure caused customer records to be retained beyond the company's 180-day policy, widening the exposure window.

crypto.title: Fireblocks Cuts 7% of Workforce After Denying Visa Acquisition Rumors
crypto.summary: Fireblocks denied Visa acquisition rumors at a ~$2.5B valuation on Thursday, then confirmed a 7% workforce reduction (60-70 jobs) the following day. The rumored deal price represents a 69% markdown from the company's $8B 2022 peak valuation, and this marks the company's third round of layoffs in recent years despite having raised approximately $1.04B in total capital. The sequence of events raises questions about the state of institutional crypto infrastructure valuations and whether Fireblocks is managing toward an exit at materially lower terms than its last primary raise. On the same day, American Express announced cutting roughly 5% of its workforce, with its CFO citing AI-driven restructuring, adding to a broader pattern of financial services firms shrinking headcount ahead of automation-driven operating model changes.

crypto.title: Morpho's fee switch can take up to 25% of borrower interest
crypto.summary: Morpho's fees are set at the market level, so they come out before curators or lenders are paid.

crypto.title: BlackRock to link tokenized MMFs with Japanese yen stablecoins
crypto.summary: BlackRock, SBI Holdings, and Startale signed an MOU to explore connecting tokenized money market funds with SBI's yen stablecoin JPYSC.

crypto.title: BitMine buys 10,452 ETH and repurchases 2.04M shares in one week
crypto.summary: BitMine's holdings rose to 6,051,933 ETH, about 4.95% of supply, with 5.23M ETH staked.

crypto.title: YC Sends $500K Seed Round to Mochatrade in USDC on Base
crypto.summary: Y Combinator sent Mochatrade's $500K seed round in USDC on Base via three transfers on a Friday evening when bank wires were unavailable, completing in seconds.

it.title: Atlassian Demo: Scale Enterprise AI Fast and Don't Break Security
it.summary: IT leaders are under pressure. They need to scale AI faster than the competition or risk losing out – but they must also protect the security, data, and governance boundaries that AI exposes to attacks, leaks, and other breaches. Atlassian's upcoming demo (Oct 29th) will reveal how to give teams AI that understands their organization's context and respects who can see what. You'll learn from end-to-end workflows for different teams: Accelerate incident response timelines in Engineering and IT. Reduce repeat questions + speed up onboarding in HR. Build accurate briefs, perform effective AI drafting & async approvals in Marketing. Save your virtual seat + get the recording.

it.title: SAP Unveils Physical AI and Extends the Autonomous Enterprise into the Real World
it.summary: SAP has unveiled its physical AI capabilities designed to connect enterprise business systems with physical operations such as robots and automated systems. At SAP TechEd, the company showcased implementations with partners like Foxconn, Arçelik-LG, Intel, and Holcim to demonstrate how business context can govern physical tasks while automatically feeding structured execution data back into enterprise workflows.

it.title: Microsoft Authenticator Flaw Exposes Work Accounts
it.summary: A patched flaw in Microsoft Authenticator for Android let malicious apps impersonate trusted Microsoft apps and obtain work-account tokens, exposing email, files, and calendars in researchers' tests. Microsoft says exploitation requires a user to complete a sign-in flow and reports no known attacks. The fix is available in version 6.2606.4246 and later.

it.title: Is it time to retire VPNs?
it.summary: As recurring vulnerabilities expose legacy VPN gateways to rapid exploitation, organizations will need to transition to zero-trust architecture. Traditional VPNs grant broad internal network access once breached, a risk amplified by AI-driven vulnerability discovery. Zero-trust models replace this perimeter approach by making internal systems invisible to the public internet and restricting users and agents to specific applications.

it.title: Closing Linux EDR Gaps
it.summary: Linux servers can show green in an EDR dashboard while collecting little or no security telemetry because of kernel incompatibilities or degraded sensor modes. Verify sensor health on each host before expanding coverage or switching vendors, then pilot changes through kernel updates and roll them out in stages. Container visibility and after-hours alert response also need explicit coverage.

it.title: 1 in 3 orgs run code assistants. Few have a governance program
it.summary: Code assistants like Cursor and Copilot are now in ~1/3 environments Field Effect protects. Unlike chat tools, they execute: downloading files and running scripts on developer endpoints with elevated permissions. Field Effect's State of AI Adoption eBook covers the implications. Read the findings, plus more insights into agents and on-device models: download the eBook.

it.title: IBM Introduces Identity and Control for AI Agents, Securing Frontier Intelligence for the Enterprise
it.summary: IBM announced new capabilities at TechXchange 2026 to provide enterprise security and governance for AI agents, combining verified identities, access controls, and performance evaluations. The updates extend HashiCorp Vault to issue short-lived credentials for non-human identities, integrate with NVIDIA OpenShell, and use watsonx Orchestrate to discover, contain, and evaluate agents across third-party platforms.

it.title: Oracle Advances Autonomous AI Lakehouse with Business Semantic Layer and Expanded Support for Iceberg Data
it.summary: Oracle is expanding its Autonomous AI Lakehouse with a Business Semantic Layer and a Business Simulation Engine designed to ground AI agents in enterprise data and improve analytical decision-making. The company also announced expanded Apache Iceberg support to simplify data management using SQL. The new capabilities are intended to help organizations scale agentic applications and improve data consistency.

it.title: From Orbit to Enterprise: The Next Tabular AI Frontier for SAP and HPE
it.summary: SAP announced plans to deploy its tabular AI foundation model, SAP-RPT, on the HPE Spaceborne Computer-2 aboard the International Space Station. The deployment aims to test real-time edge telemetry analysis, anomaly triage, and predictive maintenance in space before applying the same structured-data models to terrestrial supply chains and enterprise operations by early 2027.

it.title: Cisco Rethinks Privileged Infrastructure Access
it.summary: Cisco has introduced Privileged Infrastructure Access, a new offering designed to provide network administrators and automated agents with secure, identity-bound connections to critical network devices. The system replaces long-lived credentials and static access paths with short-lived, task-specific privileges that expire once work is completed, reducing vulnerabilities that can be exploited by AI-powered adversaries.

it.title: Tailscale Prepares SSH Security Fixes
it.summary: Tailscale is preparing patches for SSH flaws that could let authorized users exceed their assigned privileges, advising customers to tighten access policies and disable unnecessary SSH forwarding in the meantime.

it.title: Cisco, Palo Alto Networks, NTT rally after PHP2Shell crisis
it.summary: Researchers recently discovered critical vulnerabilities in the PHP programming language that exposed a vast range of enterprise products and websites to potential attacks.

hardware.title: Oracle Cloud becomes the first hyperscaler outside Google to offer TPUs, with capacity from 2027
hardware.summary: TPU capacity will be deployed in OCI's liquid-cooled data centers, tied in through Oracle's Acceleron SmartNIC fabric. Google says its eighth-generation TPU delivers up to 12.6 PFLOPS of FP4 per chip at up to 2x performance per watt, sustains over 97% goodput with optical circuit switching, and cuts network hops by over 50% for up to 80% better low-latency serving performance per dollar.

hardware.title: Cowboy Space's Big Iron rocket turns its upper stage into an orbiting megawatt-class data center
hardware.summary: Big Iron is an 86 m stainless-steel, road-transportable rocket that can carry 15,000+ kg to sun-synchronous orbit on nine 300,000 lbf methalox ‘Clydesdale' engines. The upper stage can stay in orbit as a data center with five racks of Vera Rubin GPUs, with the rocket skin doubling as the radiator and ammonia propellant as coolant. Its first flight is targeted for 2028, with up to 20,000 satellites planned pending FCC approval.

hardware.title: Anduril and Qualcomm announce BlueChip, a hardened laptop with about 90% US or allied parts
hardware.summary: BlueChip runs a Snapdragon X Series chip built at TSMC's Arizona fab, with about 90% of its bill of materials from the US or allies and a roadmap to 100% domestic. The display is one component still made only in China. It's aimed at government and military buyers rather than consumers. The chip is expected to cost about 20% more than typical high-end PCs, and open for preorder in 2027. Anduril hasn't finished contracting its suppliers.

hardware.title: Testing Silicon Photonics At Scale
hardware.summary: The push for silicon photonics in data centers requires testing infrastructure that matches evolving demands. Automated alignment and integrated optical/electrical testing are critical for overcoming challenges in coupling efficiency and throughput. Collaboration between equipment providers, developers, and manufacturers is essential to create a seamless production system for high-volume manufacturing.

hardware.title: Proposal reads an Andreev qubit's state through its supercurrent and a SQUID, with no ancilla qubits
hardware.summary: A theory paper proposes reading an Andreev qubit without ancilla qubits: its state shows up as an oscillating supercurrent in a large superconducting loop, and a small coil coupled to a SQUID picks up the magnetic signal. The method still disturbs the qubit, but within standard error-correction thresholds. It's a proposal in Physical Review B, supported by FAPESP, with no experiment yet.

hardware.title: First 32-bit MCU family built on 22nm process and featuring MRAM
hardware.summary: Renesas has launched the RX74M and RX74N, the first 32-bit MCUs using a 22nm process with embedded MRAM, reaching speeds up to 600MHz. These MCUs offer significant performance improvements and support major industrial networks like EtherCAT and TSN with integrated controllers. They enhance security with hardware-based features and support post-quantum cryptography, while a partner ecosystem aids development efficiency.

hardware.title: Fusion's supply chain could grow from $500M to over $7B by the first plants, with the tritium fuel cycle the key hurdle
hardware.summary: The fusion industry is close to delivering a roadmap to commercial power plants. The fuel cycle, especially tritium handling, is one of the most important development areas.

hardware.title: Intel to acquire quantum software maker Classiq to pair it with silicon spin-qubit chips
hardware.summary: Intel has agreed to acquire Classiq, pairing its hardware-agnostic algorithm synthesis platform with Intel's silicon spin-qubit chips and cryogenic control electronics, which Intel says it alone can make at scale on conventional fab processes. The goal is a full-stack platform that adds QPUs alongside Intel's CPUs, GPUs, and ASICs. Intel plans to keep Classiq's multi-platform integrations.

hardware.title: OpenAMRobot: Open-Source Mobile Manipulation and Physical AI Platform
hardware.summary: OpenAMRobot is an open-source, modular mobile manipulation platform designed to lower the barrier to entry for embodied AI research and hands-on imitation learning.

hardware.title: Luxonis OAK 4 FFC: Modular Multi-Camera Perception and Edge AI Platform
hardware.summary: The Luxonis OAK 4 FFC is a compact embedded vision board that pairs a 52 TOPS AI processor with five flexible camera ports on a single lightweight carrier.

hardware.title: FLoRe teaches humanoids to control contact force, and it succeeds in 80% of rollouts vs 26.7% without it
hardware.summary: Amazon FAR and university collaborators collect demonstrations without a robot, using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers plus chest and ankle trackers.

hardware.title: Agility and GXO Logistics plan expanded deployment of Digit humanoid
